html:
The Battle of Mukden was fought from late February to 10 March 1905 near Mukden, now Shenyang, in Manchuria, northeast China. The Japanese army beat the Russian army in the last and largest land battle of the Russo-Japanese War.

Japan and Russia were fighting over who would control Manchuria and Korea. After the fall of Port Arthur, Field Marshal Oyama Iwao wanted to destroy the Russian army before more troops arrived on the Trans-Siberian Railway. Japan could not afford a long war. About 250,000 Japanese faced nearly 300,000 Russians under Aleksey Kuropatkin, on a front about 150 km long. Oyama attacked in the east to draw in the Russian reserves, then sent Nogi's army around the western flank. Kuropatkin, afraid of being surrounded, ordered a retreat north. Russia lost about 90,000 men, Japan about 70,000.

It was one of the largest battles fought up to that time. Japan won the field but was too worn out to follow. After the naval Battle of Tsushima in May, both sides accepted American mediation and signed the Treaty of Portsmouth. An Asian country had beaten a European great power in a modern war, and people across Asia took note.
